1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and letter-spaced monospace for the codes, which reads well.

2.why: Instruction lines are short sentence-case text with no italics or all-caps; the only dense uppercase text sits in the Logs panel rather than in the instructions.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with large text that should map cleanly onto a phone viewport, although the screenshots only show a desktop-width render.

4.why: Each step's instruction is a single plain sentence, with only 'Base32' standing out as technical jargon.

5.why: The authenticator-code field shows no placeholder or format example, though the displayed 'Test-only current code: 627186' indirectly demonstrates the six-digit format.

6.why: To proceed at the verification step the user must read the dense multi-line monospace Logs panel to locate the six-digit test code.

7.why: No copy button or download option is offered for the Base32 secret or the recovery codes; the flow expects manual transcription ('I entered the secret').

8.why: Only a manual Base32 secret is presented; no QR code or equivalent alternative appears anywhere in the flow.

9.why: Nothing visible indicates autofill or password-manager support (no one-time-code hint on the code field), and the secret and codes are shown only as plain text.

10.why: Every screen pairs a bold heading naming the current step with a single high-contrast blue primary button that clearly stands out.

11.why: Each screen requests one primary action, with only low-emphasis secondary options such as Log out or Regenerate codes alongside it.

12.why: After each action a new card plainly states the result (e.g., the green 'MFA is active' message) and the next instruction, although fuller status detail lives in the technical Logs.

13.why: 'Regenerate codes' allows re-requesting and no penalty or lockout is shown, but there is no reveal/hide control and retry behaviour after a failed entry is never demonstrated.

14.why: No error state appears in any screenshot, so there is no observable evidence that error messages state the problem and fix without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown, expiry notice, or session timeout is visible on any screen, leaving the user free to read and enter codes at their own pace.
